metadata.title: Max Planck — The Reluctant Revolutionary
metadata.note: VOXBIO DEMO SLICE — representative first pass (4 acts, ~16 beats) authored to exercise the voxpaper skin: archival plates, portrait boxes, isotype grid, quote beats. Full 3-5 min authoring per voxbio SKILL.md. Durations are estimates until generate_audio.py runs. Facts to verify at Gate 1: von Jolly anecdote wording, Nobel 1901-1918 prize count (17, none in 1916), Erwin Planck 1945, 'act of desperation' letter (to R.W. Wood, 1931), autobiography quote.
metadata.reformat: center-cut, focus-aware; pantry/<bid>-916.* is the human replacement slot; -916 overrides honored

beats.narration_text: In 1874, a professor warned young Max Planck not to study physics — everything important, he said, had already been discovered.
beats.tts_normalized_text: In eighteen seventy-four, a professor warned young Max Planck not to study physics — everything important, he said, had already been discovered.
beats.new_visual_element: Archival plate: Munich university lecture hall, 1870s; a caption card with the professor's warning.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Plate settles; warning card slides in beneath; slow push toward the plate.

beats.narration_text: Twenty-six years later, the same man quietly broke physics in half.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Twenty-six years later, the same man quietly broke physics in half.
beats.new_visual_element: A big date card: 1900, with a thin terracotta underline — the pivot.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Date stamps on; underline draws; everything else dims a step.

beats.narration_text: This is the story of the most conservative revolutionary in the history of science.
beats.tts_normalized_text: This is the story of the most conservative revolutionary in the history of science.
beats.new_visual_element: Thesis card in serif: 'the reluctant revolutionary', golden highlighter bar behind the word reluctant.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Card slides in; highlighter bar sweeps behind the key word.

beats.narration_text: By 1900, Berlin's physicists had measured the glow of hot objects to within one percent.
beats.tts_normalized_text: By nineteen hundred, Berlin's physicists had measured the glow of hot objects to within one percent.
beats.new_visual_element: Archival plate: Berlin laboratory, blackbody apparatus; a clean measured curve overlaid on the flat plane.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Plate settles; the measured curve draws over it in dusty blue.

beats.narration_text: The best theory of the day predicted that same glow should carry infinite energy.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The best theory of the day predicted that same glow should carry infinite energy.
beats.new_visual_element: The classical prediction curve diverges off the top of the frame in terracotta; the word infinite on a highlight bar.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Second curve tracks the first, then bends violently upward and exits the frame.

beats.narration_text: Planck spent six years on that gap, and solved it only by an act he later called desperation.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Planck spent six years on that gap, and solved it only by an act he later called desperation.
beats.new_visual_element: Quote card: 'an act of desperation' — small grey attribution, letter to R. W. Wood, 1931.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Quote card settles between the curves; attribution fades in under it.

beats.narration_text: He assumed energy comes in discrete packets — and the infinity simply vanished.
beats.tts_normalized_text: He assumed energy comes in discrete packets — and the infinity simply vanished.
beats.new_visual_element: Equation card: E = hν on white, hairline frame; the diverging curve folds back down onto the measured one.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Equation stamps on; terracotta curve relaxes onto the blue one.

beats.narration_text: He did not believe the packets were real — he hoped for years the trick would go away.
beats.tts_normalized_text: He did not believe the packets were real — he hoped for years the trick would go away.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Hold on the equation; highlight pulses once on E = hν.

beats.narration_text: It took Albert Einstein to take Planck's trick seriously as a fact about light itself.
beats.tts_normalized_text: It took Albert Einstein to take Planck's trick seriously as a fact about light itself.
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait box: Einstein 1905; card: 'light itself comes in quanta' — Planck resisted this for years.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Portrait settles beside a contrast card; the two positions labeled walls versus light.

beats.narration_text: The prize committee eventually sided with the reluctant man from Berlin.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The prize committee eventually sided with the reluctant man from Berlin.
beats.new_visual_element: Isotype grid: the Nobel Prizes in Physics awarded 1901-1918, Planck's marked in terracotta.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Dot grid counts up in reading order, timed to the narration; Planck's dot lands last.

viz.label: Nobel Prizes in Physics, 1901–1918
viz.note: 17 prizes in 18 years — none awarded 1916. Verify before final.

beats.narration_text: Nineteen eighteen: the Nobel Prize, for the quantum he never wanted.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Nineteen eighteen: the Nobel Prize, for the quantum he never wanted.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Hold; the terracotta dot pulses once.

beats.narration_text: The century he opened treated him brutally — war took one son, and the Gestapo executed another in 1945.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The century he opened treated him brutally — war took one son, and the Gestapo executed another in nineteen forty-five.
beats.new_visual_element: Archival plate: Berlin 1945, ruins; small date card. Restraint: no dramatization, one plate, one date.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Plate settles slowly; date card fades in; nothing else moves.

beats.narration_text: Near the end he wrote that a new truth does not triumph by convincing its opponents, but because its opponents eventually die.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Near the end he wrote that a new truth does not triumph by convincing its opponents, but because its opponents eventually die.
beats.new_visual_element: Quote card, serif, golden highlight on 'a new scientific truth'; attribution: Scientific Autobiography, 1948.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Quote writes on line by line; highlight bar sweeps once.

beats.narration_text: Max Planck opened a door he spent his whole life trying to close — and physics walked through it.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Max Planck opened a door he spent his whole life trying to close — and physics walked through it.
beats.new_visual_element: Closing portrait box of Planck, older; the equation returns small beneath it.
beats.video_animation_prompt: Portrait settles; equation fades in under; slow settle to stillness.

beats.narration_text: Part of the Bears Notes series.
